evidence: What is exercised well: every gate, Functional and Polish criterion is an action sequence, not a first-paint read. Waits are explicit (functional/judge.toml:272 'Wait at least six more seconds', :281 same, :263 'within about ten seconds', :344 'watch its library for up to ten seconds', :362 'Within ten seconds') and functional/prompt.md:24 says 'Where waiting is required, wait the stated time; do not shorten it'. Viewport behaviour is exercised: polish/judge.toml:68 'Resize the browser viewport to about 390 by 844 pixels and reload ... type a one-line program in the editor, Run it ... Restore the desktop viewport afterwards', matching ui.md:17. Focus and disabled-state toggling are exercised (polish/judge.toml:23, :41, :50, :59). The brief requires no theme or animation, so no theme toggle is owed. Defect: the Visual dimension scores two interaction-dependent, time-varying states from a screen it never tells the judge to produce. visual/judge.toml:24 asks the judge to assess 'the visibility of the caret and of a selection', and anchor :25 ('caret and selection easy to see') makes both a condition of a 5. The only setup in visual/prompt.md:10 is 'put a ten-line JavaScript draft in the editor and Run it once'; nothing tells the judge to click back into the editor, create a selection, or look at the caret more than once. No selection exists after that setup, and ui.md:17 returns focus to the code after Format, Undo, Redo, a replacement or Save, not after Run, so focus may sit on the Run control. The caret is also time-varying in the reference itself: solution/app/src/style.css:18 'animation:cw-caret 1s step-end infinite' with :20 '@keyframes cw-caret{50%{opacity:0}}', so the caret is invisible for half of every second and a single screenshot shows it only about half the time. Run evidence: the raw-evidence index states 'Visual ratings, judge duration, Oracle reward and reward discrimination are not measured', and the scripted suite takes its 1440 screenshot (polish.cjs:125) without scoring caret or selection, so no run touches this finding. The hashes of all indexed artifacts match.
counterexample: Conforming app that can lose credit: the golden (or any app with a normal blinking caret that hides the caret or dims the selection while the editor is unfocused) is screenshotted right after clicking Run; no selection exists and the caret is in its off phase or the editor is blurred, so a judge following the prompt literally sees neither and rates cw_visual_editor_readability 3 or 4 instead of 5, or rates it differently on a rerun depending on blink phase. Weak app that can gain credit: an app whose selection highlight is nearly invisible (for example a background one shade from the editor background) is never asked to show a selection, so a judge that scores the still at 5 gives it full credit for a selection treatment it never saw.
suggested_fix: In tests/scored/visual/prompt.md (setup line 10) or in cw_visual_editor_readability, tell the judge to click inside the editor after Run, select a word with a double click or Shift+Arrow, and observe the caret over at least two screenshots or about two seconds because a caret may blink, before rating caret and selection visibility; alternatively drop caret and selection from that criterion and its 5 anchor. Either change invalidates the current clearance and needs a fresh candidate.
